title: Detroit Root Network
subtitle: An agentic development case study for Detroit
summary: A deployed community food discovery and farm operations beta that connects local availability, selling locations, inventory updates, and volunteer opportunities in one application.
pitch: Detroit Root Network starts with a practical question: where can someone find locally grown food, and is the information current enough to act on? We built a shared discovery experience and a simple operations workspace so growers can maintain the information customers need. The project demonstrates how product leadership, technical business analysis, program management, and UX research can guide AI-assisted development from requirements through a working cloud deployment. The next step is a controlled farmer pilot to measure whether the workflows improve information freshness and ease of use.

capabilities.title: Food discovery
capabilities.body: Search farms and produce, filter by Detroit region, in-stock items, selling now, and volunteer opportunities, and open detailed stall cards from the list or map.

capabilities.title: Farm operations
capabilities.body: Update farm details and selling schedules, add or edit inventory, select standardized units, adjust quantity and price, and mark produce sold out.

capabilities.title: Volunteer coordination
capabilities.body: Publish opportunities with a description, date, and volunteer count. Mobile form refinements include persistent labels, wider fields, aligned controls, and a 500-character description limit.

capabilities.title: Product feedback
capabilities.body: Capture page and element context with feedback, review saved notes, and export CSV backups for product review.

stack: App Router pages and server route handlers connect a responsive browser experience to authentication services.
Typed data models and responsive styling support discovery, operations, and feedback workflows. Tailwind 4 is included in the styling toolchain.
Persistent relational records, email magic links, authenticated sessions, profile roles, farm memberships, and database access policies.
Row Level Security and SQL triggers
Database policies govern access. T2 fixture protection checks both old and new records, including tier changes and child-record moves.
Interactive Detroit map with clickable, seeded farm markers. Current markers use predefined coordinates rather than automatic geocoding.
PowerShell build and Git workflow, automatic deployment from main, environment-scoped configuration, and firewall rules.
ESLint, TypeScript, Node tests, PostgreSQL tools
Production builds, focused authentication tests, and a database backup whose archive contents were checked before migration.

flows.title: Discovery to action
steps: A visitor filters farms or selects a map marker.
The app displays produce, selling details, payment methods, and volunteer information.
The visitor can open directions or use the posted information to plan a visit.

flows.title: Authorized operations
steps: The application loads the profile role and farm memberships.
Browser writes use the public Supabase client with the user's session; RLS and triggers enforce access.
The interface reloads affected data after confirmed changes.

flows.title: Release to production
steps: Requirements and acceptance criteria guide a scoped change.
Lint, authentication tests, and the production build run locally.
Selected files are committed and pushed to GitHub main.
Vercel builds the deployment; environment changes require redeployment.
The team validates the live workflow and permissions.

configuration: Confirmed existing identities; applied migration 005; verified Owner and Director Q profile roles; configured production Site URL and the email callback redirect. Q's Stall membership and cross-T1 policies are included in the migration.
Configured public Supabase connection values and private server variables; enabled a temporary beta-login kill switch; published a firewall rate-limit rule before enabling code access.
Used the existing repository and main branch; staged specific deployment files; ran validation and pushed commit 8175d66 for the beta-authentication release.

Installed PostgreSQL command-line tools, created a database archive through the session pooler, and successfully listed the archive before applying the migration. A full restore rehearsal remains a next step.

decisions.title: Roles are enforced in the database
decisions.body: Owner and Director Q can work across T1 stalls, while farmers use membership-based access. A hidden button is not treated as an authorization control.

decisions.title: Editable trials and discovery fixtures are separated
decisions.body: T1 stalls support operational testing. T2 stalls populate discovery without permitting app users to modify those records, even by changing tiers or moving child records.

decisions.title: Temporary convenience has an exit requirement
decisions.body: Owner and Director Q beta codes are validated on the server and exchanged for normal Supabase sessions. Codes remain private configuration, and the entire code-login pathway must be removed before a larger demo.

decisions.title: Human judgment directs agentic development
decisions.body: AI tools helped produce and revise implementation, tests, SQL, and deployment instructions. The project team set the scope, evaluated the experience, configured services, and accepted or corrected the results.

evidence: Vercel deployment reached Ready, and the project owner reported successful beta-code login and satisfactory access checks.

The beta-authentication release passed lint, a production build, and eight route tests covering failed and successful authentication boundaries. These tests mock Supabase; they are not a complete live RLS audit.
Migration 005 completed successfully. Owner and Director Q roles were confirmed in the profiles table.
The production Site URL and callback allowlist were corrected after a failed return and email rate-limit error. A successful post-correction email sign-in still needs confirmation.
A pilot of up to 15 farmers is planned. No adoption, revenue, yield, or food-access impact metrics are claimed yet.

demo: Start with the public discovery page and filter for available produce.
Open a stall card and its mapped location.
Have an authorized presenter demonstrate a T1 inventory update and the refreshed listing.

recruiterSummary: This project demonstrates senior delivery leadership across product definition, technical requirements, role design, cloud configuration, release validation, operational recovery, and an evolving user experience. Its strongest evidence is a working integration and documented decisions; community impact is the next hypothesis to validate.
